method_card.title: Cumulative Frequency, Box Plots & Histograms
method_card.content:
Cumulative frequency (CF): Running total of frequencies. Plot at upper class boundaries and join with a smooth curve. Read off: median at \(n/2\), Q1 at \(n/4\), Q3 at \(3n/4\). IQR = Q3 − Q1.

Box plots: Show min, Q1, median, Q3, max. The box spans the IQR. Useful for comparing distributions.

Histograms: Use frequency density on the y-axis. FD = frequency ÷ class width. The area of each bar = frequency. Unequal class widths are standard.
method_card.example:
CF of 60 values: Q1 at 15th = 22, Median at 30th = 35, Q3 at 45th = 48.

IQR = 48 − 22 = 26.

gold.display: The histogram shows ages of visitors. Estimate the number of visitors aged between 15 and 25.

misconceptions.message: 15 to 25 is only part of each bar. Use the part widths (5 each): 4 × 5 = 20 and 3 × 5 = 15, giving 35, not the whole bars (40 + 30 = 70).

gold.hint: The range 15 to 25 covers parts of two bars; find each part with FD times width and add.

guided_steps.say: 15 to 25 spans parts of two bars. Find each part's frequency with FD × width, then add.

guided_steps.pre: The 15 to 20 part sits in the 10 to 20 bar (FD 4), width 5. Frequency = 4 × 5 =
The 20 to 25 part sits in the 20 to 30 bar (FD 3), width 5. Frequency = 3 × 5 =

guided_steps.done: An estimated 35 visitors were aged between 15 and 25.

gold.display: The CF curve shows results for 120 students. The pass mark is set so that 75% of students pass. Estimate the pass mark from the graph.

misconceptions.message: 90 is the number who pass (75% of 120), not a score. The pass mark is the score with 25% (30 students) below it: read where cumulative frequency = 30, giving 30.

gold.hint: If 75% pass, 25% fail; find the score with that many students below it.

guided_steps.say: If 75% pass, 25% fail. The pass mark is the score with 25% of students below it.

guided_steps.pre: So 30 students are below the pass mark. On the curve, the cumulative frequency we look for is =
Read down from cumulative frequency 30 to the score axis. Pass mark =
guided_steps.done: At a score of 30 the cumulative frequency is 30, so 90 students (75%) score above it.

gold.display: A histogram has bars: 0-10 (FD=3), 10-25 (FD=4), 25-30 (FD=6), 30-50 (FD=2). Find the modal class.

misconceptions.message: With unequal classes the modal class has the highest frequency density (FD 6 in 25-30), not the highest frequency. 10-25 has the most values (60) but a lower bar.

gold.hint: The modal class has the highest frequency density, not the highest frequency.

gold.display: A histogram: 0-20 (FD=2), 20-30 (FD=5), 30-50 (FD=3). Estimate the median class.

misconceptions.message: The median class holds the middle value, not the largest frequency. Frequencies 40, 50, 60 total 150; the 75th value sits in 20-30 (cumulative 90 there), so 30-50 is wrong.

gold.hint: Find each class frequency (FD times width), then locate the class holding the middle value.

gold.display: Compare the two box plots. By how much does Class B's median exceed Class A's?

misconceptions.message: Take Class B's median minus Class A's: 50 − 40 = 10. Doing 40 − 50 gives −10; the question asks how much B exceeds A.

gold.hint: Read each median line, then subtract the smaller from the larger.

guided_steps.say: Read each median, the line inside each box, then subtract.

guided_steps.pre: Class A median (line inside the lower box) =
Class B median (line inside the upper box) =

guided_steps.done: Class B's median is 10 marks above Class A's.

bronze.display: The cumulative frequency curve shows scores for 80 students. Read the median score from the graph.

misconceptions.message: 40 is the position (n ÷ 2), not the median score. Read across from cumulative frequency 40 to the curve, then down to the score: about 45.

bronze.hint: The median is at position n divided by 2; read across from that cumulative frequency.

guided_steps.say: The median is the middle value, half way through the data.

guided_steps.pre: Read across from cumulative frequency 40 to the curve, then down. Median score =
guided_steps.hint: It sits half way between 40 and 50.
guided_steps.done: At score 45 the cumulative frequency is 40, half of 80, so 45 is the median.

bronze.display: The box plot shows test scores. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?

misconceptions.message: That is the range (max − min = 80 − 20 = 60). The IQR is the box width: Q3 − Q1 = 55 − 35 = 20.

bronze.hint: IQR is the width of the box: right side minus left side.

guided_steps.say: The IQR is the width of the box: Q3 − Q1.

guided_steps.pre: Read Q3, the right side of the box =
Read Q1, the left side of the box =

guided_steps.done: 20 is the spread of the middle half of the data.

bronze.display: The box plot shows heights of students. What is the median height?

misconceptions.message: The median is not the middle of the range. Read the line inside the box: 168, not (150 + 190) ÷ 2 = 170.

bronze.hint: The median is the line inside the box.

guided_steps.say: The median is the line drawn inside the box.

guided_steps.pre: Read Q1, the left edge of the box =
Read Q3, the right edge of the box =
The median is the line inside the box, between 160 and 175. Read it =
guided_steps.hint: Look for the line splitting the box.
guided_steps.done: 168 lies between 160 and 175, so it sits inside the box, as it must.

bronze.display: The cumulative frequency curve shows waiting times for 60 patients. Find Q1.

misconceptions.message: 15 is the position (n ÷ 4), not the value. Read across from cumulative frequency 15 to the curve, then down: Q1 is about 8 minutes.

bronze.hint: Q1 is at position n divided by 4; read across from that cumulative frequency.

guided_steps.say: Q1 is the lower quartile: a quarter of the way through the data.

guided_steps.pre: Read across from cumulative frequency 15 to the curve, then down. Q1 =
guided_steps.hint: It lands between 5 and 10 minutes, near 8.
guided_steps.done: At about 8 minutes the cumulative frequency is roughly 15, a quarter of 60.

bronze.display: The box plot shows the range of weights. What is the range?

misconceptions.message: That is the IQR (Q3 − Q1 = 70 − 50 = 20). The range is max − min = 80 − 40 = 40.

bronze.hint: Range is the distance between the two whisker ends: max minus min.

guided_steps.say: The range is the full spread: max − min, from whisker end to whisker end.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the smallest from the largest.
guided_steps.done: 40 kg is the full spread of the weights.

bronze.display: A histogram bar has frequency density 5 and class width 5. Find the frequency.

misconceptions.message: Frequency is FD × width = 5 × 5 = 25, not FD ÷ width. Multiply, because the frequency is the area of the bar.

bronze.hint: Frequency is the area of the bar: FD times class width.

guided_steps.say: On a histogram, frequency = frequency density × class width (the area of the bar).

guided_steps.done: 25 is the number of items in that class.

bronze.display: A histogram bar represents 30 items and has class width 10. Find the frequency density.

misconceptions.message: FD = frequency ÷ width = 30 ÷ 10 = 3, not frequency × width. Divide to get the bar height.

bronze.hint: Frequency density is frequency divided by class width.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange: frequency density = frequency ÷ class width.

guided_steps.done: 3 is the height of the bar on the frequency density axis.

bronze.display: A box plot has Q1 = 25 and Q3 = 55. Find the IQR.

misconceptions.message: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 55 − 25 = 30. Subtract the quartiles, do not add them.

guided_steps.done: 30 is the width of the middle half of the data.

silver.display: The CF curve shows data for 100 students. Estimate the number of students who scored between 30 and 50.

misconceptions.message: 55 is the number scoring up to 50. Subtract those scoring up to 30 (which is 15): 55 − 15 = 40.

silver.hint: Read the cumulative frequency at each mark, then subtract the smaller from the larger.

guided_steps.say: To count how many lie between two values, read the cumulative frequency at each and subtract.

guided_steps.pre: Read the cumulative frequency at mark 30 =
guided_steps.hint: Go up from 30 to the curve.

guided_steps.pre: Read the cumulative frequency at mark 50 =
guided_steps.hint: Go up from 50 to the curve.

silver.display: The two box plots compare Class A and Class B. Which class performed more consistently?

misconceptions.message: Class B has the larger IQR (35 versus 15), so Class B is less consistent. The smaller box, Class A, is more consistent.

silver.hint: Compare the box widths: a smaller IQR means more consistent.

silver.display: The histogram shows waiting times. How many people waited between 10 and 20 minutes? (FD × class width = frequency)

misconceptions.message: 3 is the frequency density, the bar height. Frequency = FD × width = 3 × 10 = 30 people.

silver.hint: Frequency equals frequency density times the class width.

guided_steps.say: Read the bar's frequency density, then frequency = FD × width.

guided_steps.pre: Frequency density of the 10 to 20 bar =

silver.display: A CF curve shows Q1 = 28, median = 42, Q3 = 56. Find the IQR.

misconceptions.message: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 56 − 28 = 28. Subtract the quartiles, do not add them (56 + 28 = 84).
The IQR ignores the median. It is Q3 − Q1 = 56 − 28 = 28, not 56 − 42 = 14.

silver.hint: IQR uses only the quartiles: Q3 minus Q1.

guided_steps.say: The IQR uses only the quartiles: Q3 − Q1. The median is not needed.

guided_steps.done: 28 is the spread of the middle half.

silver.display: A histogram has classes 0-5 (FD=2), 5-10 (FD=6), 10-20 (FD=3), 20-40 (FD=1). Find the total frequency.

misconceptions.message: You added the frequency densities (2 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 12). Multiply each by its class width first: 10 + 30 + 30 + 20 = 90.

silver.hint: Work out each bar's frequency with FD times width, then add them all.

guided_steps.say: Total frequency = the sum of (FD × width) for every bar.

guided_steps.done: 90 is the total number of values.

silver.display: Draw conclusions: Box plot A has median 50 and IQR 10. Box plot B has median 55 and IQR 30. Which statement is correct?
options: B has a higher average but A is more consistent
A has a higher average and is more consistent
B is better in every way

misconceptions.message: B has the higher median but the larger IQR (30 versus 10), so B is less consistent, not better in every way. A is the more consistent set.

silver.hint: A higher median means a higher average; a smaller IQR means more consistent.

silver.display: From a CF diagram with 200 data points, estimate how many are above 65 if CF at 65 is 140.

misconceptions.message: 140 is how many scored 65 or below. Above 65 = total − 140 = 200 − 140 = 60.

silver.hint: Above a value equals the total minus the cumulative frequency at that value.

guided_steps.say: 'Above 65' = the total minus how many are 65 or below (the cumulative frequency at 65).

problem_bank.silver_description: Combine two readings: gaps on a cumulative frequency curve, histogram frequencies, and comparisons of two distributions.

bronze.title: Bronze: reading a single value from a chart
steps: On a box plot: the middle line is the median, the box edges are Q1 and Q3, the whisker ends are the minimum and maximum.
IQR = Q3 − Q1 (the box width). Range = max − min (whisker to whisker).
On a histogram: frequency = frequency density × class width. Rearranged, FD = frequency ÷ width.

silver.title: Silver: combining two readings
steps: Between two values on a cumulative frequency curve: read the CF at each and subtract.
For a histogram frequency, do FD × width for each bar; add them for a total.
To compare two distributions, compare the medians (average) and the IQRs (spread: smaller is more consistent).

gold.title: Gold: estimating and working back
steps: Part of a bar: use the part's width, not the whole class. Frequency = FD × part width.
From a percentage: turn it into a count (percentage of the total), then read the matching score on the curve.
Modal class = tallest bar by frequency density. The median class holds the middle value once the frequencies are listed.
